quote: the seven major principles and sixty-two specific techniques that were most likely to prove needful in the Ritual Of Changing One’s Mind
content: The room in the story has two people in it, one of them hostile: Jeffreyssai is running the ritual on his student, and the whole sequence of which this is the coda is about instruction, criticism and the school. That is the social structure the annotation says the book should have drawn, drawn. What is fair in the charge is that the ritual itself is depicted as an internal act with an examiner rather than an adversarial collaboration; the corrected picture is the beisutsukai school, which the fiction elsewhere supplies, and the sequence's later community-building was an attempt to construct exactly that. The two-in-seven figure is invented and the essay presents it as fiction.
